/-!
# Conjecture 4.33

by M. I. Kargapolov

Let $\mathfrak{K}_n$ be the class of all groups with a single defining relation in the
variety of soluble groups of derived length $n$.

a) Under what conditions does a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group have non-trivial centre? Can a
$\mathfrak{K}_n$-group, $n \geq 2$, that cannot be generated by two elements have
non-trivial centre? *Editors' comment (1998):* These questions were answered for $n = 2$
(E. I. Timoshenko, *Siberian Math. J.*, **14**, no. 6 (1973), 954–957; *Math. Notes*,
**64**, no. 6 (1998), 798–803).

b) Describe the abelian subgroups of $\mathfrak{K}_n$-groups.

c) Investigate the periodic subgroups of $\mathfrak{K}_n$-groups.

Only the yes/no question of part a) is formalised here. The first question of a) and parts
b) and c) ask for a description or an investigation and have no statable proposition.

A group $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{K}_n$ if $G \cong \langle X \mid r \rangle_{\mathfrak{A}^n}$
for some set $X$ and some word $r$ in the free group $F(X)$, where $\mathfrak{A}^n$ is the
variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $n$. Concretely,
$G \cong F(X) / F(X)^{(n)} \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$, where $F(X)^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th
derived subgroup of $F(X)$ (the verbal subgroup of $\mathfrak{A}^n$) and
$\langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ is the normal closure of $r$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup (n : ℕ) (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (r : FreeGroup ι),
    Nonempty
      (G ≃* FreeGroup ι ⧸ (derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}))

justification.closest_existing_considered: PresentedGroup (would require passing the whole set ↑(derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n) ∪ {r} as relators, which is equivalent but less transparent); derivedSeries / IsSolvable (used, but they give no presentation-theoretic notion); FreeGroup + QuotientGroup (used as building blocks). Searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for OneRelator/FreeSolvable/Metabelian — nothing found.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.33».IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a relatively free group of a variety, nor of a one-relator group in a variety. The class 𝔎ₙ is defined directly: G ≅ FreeGroup ι ⧸ (derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}) for some type ι and relator r. Two @[category test] lemmas (the free soluble group F/δₙ(F) is a 𝔎ₙ-group; every 𝔎ₙ-group is IsSolvable) are proved to sanity-check the definition.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isOneRelatorSolubleGroup_free (ι : Type u) (n : ℕ) :
    IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup n (FreeGroup ι ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n) := by
  refine ⟨ι, 1, ⟨QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq ?_⟩⟩
  have : Subgroup.normalClosure ({1} : Set (FreeGroup ι)) = ⊥ :=
    le_antisymm (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp)) bot_le
  rw [this, sup_bot_eq]
blocks.docstring:
The free soluble group of derived length $n$ on a set $X$ (the trivial relation $r = 1$)
is a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup.derivedSeries_eq_bot {n : ℕ} {G : Type u} [Group G]
    (hG : IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup n G) : derivedSeries G n = ⊥ := by
  obtain ⟨ι, r, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG
  set N := derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}
  have hN : derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι ⧸ N) n = ⊥ := by
    rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective N), Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff,
      QuotientGroup.ker_mk']
    exact le_sup_left
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective, hN, Subgroup.map_bot]

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.33».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G), 2 ≤ n ∧ IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup n G ∧
      (¬ ∃ a b : G, Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤) ∧ Subgroup.center G ≠ ⊥ := by

blocks.docstring:
Can a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group, $n \geq 2$, that cannot be generated by two elements have
non-trivial centre?

Here a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group is a group with a single defining relation in the variety of
soluble groups of derived length $n$ (see `IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup`). The question is read as
asking whether there exist some $n \geq 2$ and some $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group $G$ such that no two
elements of $G$ generate $G$ and the centre of $G$ is non-trivial. "Cannot be generated by two
elements" is a property of the abstract group, not of its presentation. The restriction
$n \geq 2$ excludes the abelian case $n = 1$, where for instance
$\mathbb{Z}^3 \in \mathfrak{K}_1$ is not generated by two elements and equals its own centre.
The case $n = 2$ was answered by Timoshenko (1973, 1998).

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n ≥ 2 and a group G ≅ (F/derivedSeries F n)/normalClosure {r} (F free, r a single relator; derived length n means the variety identity δ_n = 1, i.e. length ≤ n) such that G is not generated by any two elements (a property of the abstract group, not of the presentation) and Subgroup.center G ≠ ⊥; n ≥ 2 excludes the trivial abelian case n = 1, the quantifier over n could alternatively be read per fixed n, and the case n = 2 is already settled by Timoshenko (1973, 1998) so only n ≥ 3 is genuinely open.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates assert the same proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n ≥ 2 and a group G ≅ F(ι)/(F(ι)^{(n)}·⟨⟨r⟩⟩) (single relator in the variety 𝔄ⁿ, encoded via Mathlib's derivedSeries) such that no two elements generate G (abstract-group property) and Subgroup.center G ≠ ⊥. I checked: answer(True) is the positive answer; quantifiers are all after answer(); the 2-generation clause allows a = b so cyclic/trivial groups are excluded as intended; r = 1 (free soluble groups) cannot be a witness so admitting it is harmless; the join quotient F/(F^{(n)} ⊔ ⟨⟨r⟩⟩) coincides with the nested quotient (F/F^{(n)})/⟨⟨r̄⟩⟩ used by c03/c04/c07/c08. The finite-rank restriction in c02 versus arbitrary generating type elsewhere does not change the yes/no answer: a non-trivial central element of an infinitely generated 𝔎ₙ-group lies in the retract ⟨Y | r⟩_{𝔄ⁿ} for a finite Y ⊇ supp(r) ∪ supp(z) with |Y| ≥ 4, which is a finitely generated non-2-generated 𝔎ₙ-group with the same central element. c01 was chosen for packaging: a universe-polymorphic bespoke predicate with a clear docstring, a test theorem, and theorem naming matching the existing Kourovka files (kourovka.«N» inside namespace Kourovka.«N»). Edits: replaced c01's IsSolvable test by the stronger derivedSeries_eq_bot API lemma (adapted from c05), and expanded the main docstring to spell out the existential reading over n and the Z³ example for why n = 1 is excluded (from c02).

/--
Can a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group, $n \geq 2$, that cannot be generated by two elements have
non-trivial centre?

Here a $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group is a group with a single defining relation in the variety of
soluble groups of derived length $n$ (see `IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup`). The question is read as
asking whether there exist some $n \geq 2$ and some $\mathfrak{K}_n$-group $G$ such that no two
elements of $G$ generate $G$ and the centre of $G$ is non-trivial. "Cannot be generated by two
elements" is a property of the abstract group, not of its presentation. The restriction
$n \geq 2$ excludes the abelian case $n = 1$, where for instance

-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.33».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : Type) (_ : Group G), 2 ≤ n ∧ IsOneRelatorSolubleGroup n G ∧
      (¬ ∃ a b : G, Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤) ∧ Subgroup.center G ≠ ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.33»

items: The generating set of the presentation is an arbitrary type ι (same universe as G), not restricted to be finite. This is the literal reading of 'the class of all groups with a single defining relation'. It is equivalent, as a yes/no question, to the finitely generated reading: if some f.g. example exists both readings say yes; if no f.g. non-2-generated 𝔎ₙ-group has non-trivial centre, then neither does an infinitely generated one, since a central element z lies in ⟨S⟩ for a finite S ⊇ supp(r) with |S| ≥ 4, and ⟨S⟩ ≅ ⟨S | r⟩_{𝔄ⁿ} is a retract of G, hence a f.g. non-2-generated 𝔎ₙ-group in which z is central.

'Derived length n' is read as membership in the variety 𝔄ⁿ (derived length ≤ n), encoded by quotienting F(ι) by derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) n; a 𝔎ₙ-group may have smaller derived length. This follows the decomposition notes.

The relator r is arbitrary, including r = 1 (so free soluble groups count as 𝔎ₙ-groups with a trivial relation). This does not affect the question: free soluble groups of rank ≥ 3 and n ≥ 1 have trivial centre and free soluble groups of rank ≤ 2 are 2-generated.

'Cannot be generated by two elements' is formalised as ¬ ∃ a b : G, Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤, a property of the abstract group (it also excludes cyclic and trivial groups, which are generated by ≤ 2 elements), not of the presentation.

Following the decomposition table, the quantifier over n is existential (∃ n ≥ 2) inside a single answer(sorry) ↔ …, rather than a per-n family of questions. The docstring records that n = 2 is settled by Timoshenko and that n ≥ 2 excludes the abelian case n = 1.
The theorem quantifies G : Type (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files; the predicate itself is universe-polymorphic.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) The quantifier over n is read existentially (∃ n ≥ 2), as the decomposition table prescribes; a per-fixed-n family is the alternative reading. The existential form stays open only because Timoshenko's n = 2 answer was negative (metabelian one-relator groups that are not 2-generated have trivial centre), consistent with the notebook still listing the problem as unsolved; had the n = 2 answer been positive the existential statement would already be settled. (2) 'Derived length n' is read as the variety 𝔄ⁿ (derived length ≤ n), the only reading under which it is a variety; 𝔎ₙ-groups may have derived length < n. (3) The generating set is an arbitrary type rather than finite; as argued in per_slot this is equivalent for the yes/no question. Dropped parts ('under what conditions', 'describe', 'investigate') have no statable Prop and were not formalized; all candidates agreed. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning; intended path in the repo would be FormalConjectures/Kourovka/4_33.lean.
